# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My thinking: I'm Mute — my only channel is gestures to Deaf. I can't reach Blind at all, so everything I know must flow through Deaf, who can speak to both Blind and me (I'll hear Deaf's speech at the start of round 2). What I hold so far: the light walks a fixed circle of five colours, one row of the mapping is in hand (orange light → cut blue wire), and more rows should arrive in later rounds. None of this means anything to Deaf yet — gestures carry no built-in meaning, and I have no way to name colours. So the right first move is to open the channel and propose cooperation rather than send an undecodable sequence: a wave for attention, the writing hand to signal "I hold written instructions — the manual", and the handshake to say "let's build a code together". Deaf can see the bomb and the light, and can talk; once Deaf proposes a protocol, I can answer with gestures in round 2 and we can start moving real mappings through.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, and you are my only link: I can hear you but never see gestures, and Deaf can never hear words at all — so everything visual must reach Deaf through your hands, and everything reaches me only through your voice. What my hands find: one display, one light, and exactly three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, and nothing else — no buttons or other modules. Positions feel solid and distinct, but colours, printing, the display's text and the light's state are all invisible to me. Please read me the manual section covering a display, a light and three wires, then tell me exactly what Deaf must report — I expect wire colours per position, the display's text, and whether the light is lit or dark. I have gestured Deaf a counting seed, 1 then 2 then 3 by finger count, so wire positions and digits can be tagged by number; open hand versus closed fist may serve for the light if Deaf picks it up. When you know the answer, name the position number or numbers to cut and the order. I will not cut anything until you say so.
Blind gestures: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

My thinking: Round 2, I act first. Key structural facts: I cannot speak, so Blind's request for me to "read the manual aloud" is impossible — the only voice Deaf and Blind can both use is Deaf's, and crucially nothing says I can't *hear*: Deaf can talk, and I will receive it. So the real circuit is: Blind → Deaf (speech), Deaf → me (speech), me → Deaf (gestures), Deaf → Blind (speech). My manual is the only source of the light→wire rule, but the manual must reach Deaf in signed form, since Deaf applies it directly to what Deaf sees (light colour, wire colours per position) and then just tells Blind a position number — Blind never needs colour words at all.

There's also a latency trap: the light changes every round, and Blind can only cut after Deaf speaks, so any cut uses one-round-old light info. Later, once Deaf has observed the fixed five-colour cycle and I've passed the full table, Deaf can *predict* the next round's colour and pre-order the cut. For now: bootstrap. Deaf already saw my 👋✍🤝 and Blind's finger-count seed, so I echo the seed to confirm it (☝✌🤟 = 1, 2, 3 = wire positions), adopt Blind's lit/dark proposal (✋/✊), propose the near-universal 👍/👎 as yes/no, and press 🤙 twice — "call me, speak to me" — because the single most important thing Deaf can learn right now is that I hear speech and will answer by hand.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍", "🤙", "👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "✋", "✊", "🫵", "🤙"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, blind again — I have heard nothing from anyone yet, so I repeat the essentials, shorter. Your voice is the only channel that reaches me at all. My hands hold: one display, one light, three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, nothing else on the casing. Remember that Deaf can speak — only Deaf's hearing is gone — so the fastest chain needs no hands at all: Deaf says aloud the colour of wire 1, 2 and 3, what the display reads, and whether the light is lit; you hear that, match it against the manual, then speak me the position number to cut, one cut at a time, and wait for my confirmation before the next. If Deaf stays silent instead, fall back to gesturing Deaf questions and voicing me the results. I will not touch the cutters until a number comes out of your mouth.
Blind gestures: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤏 🙏]
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf speaking. You hear me, so I will only use speech to you — my hands add nothing. First, my world: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, ever. If you want anything from me, you must gesture it; I see your gestures. BOMB REPORT: display reads 0. The light was white last round and is yellow this round — it changed between rounds. Three wires: position 1 green, position 2 red, position 3 blue. That is everything printed or lit that I can see. CODE PROPOSAL, memorize it: thumbs up = yes, thumbs down = no, one finger = 1, two fingers = 2, three fingers = 3, call-me = repeat/again, point-at-you = 'I address you, Deaf', open palm = stop. Color tokens: point-left = green, point-right = red, point-up = blue, five fingers = white, five fingers other hand = yellow. If you accept this code, gesture me thumbs up next round; if a token is wrong, gesture thumbs down and re-teach just that one. I will report any visual change every round.

My thinking: Round 3 and the circuit is finally live — Deaf speaks, I hear it. Two big lessons from this round's arrivals. First, Deaf talks but addresses everything `to="mute"`, and Deaf has no idea anyone else can hear — Blind, who is waiting for a number "out of my mouth", has literally never heard Deaf's voice, and doesn't know I *can't* speak. Until Deaf's speech reaches Blind, the defusal chain has no last link. Second, a timing trap: within a round the order is Mute → Blind → Deaf, so any cut Blind performs happens *after* Deaf's same-round report — meaning the light Deaf sees while speaking is not the light at the moment of the cut. Since the light "walks the same circle of five colours", Deaf will eventually need to predict the next colour, but I only know fragments so far: light was white in round 1, yellow in round 2, and my manual so far holds exactly one row — orange light → cut blue wire. With no row for yellow and no known successor, no cut is safe this round.

So my payload to Deaf: accept the proposed code (👍), flag the one collision Deaf built in — ☝ is already "1", so blue must be the backhand point 👆 (👎 = wrong, then the fix, exactly the repair procedure Deaf itself proposed) — then teach a new token 👌 = orange and pass my first manual row twice in a stable format, colour ✊(cut) colour: orange→blue, orange→blue. Then ✋: hold, no cut this round. Then the redirect that matters most: 🙏 (the hand Blind itself kept gesturing) + 👐 (everyone) + speech + cut + 1-2-3 — "voice your reports and cut orders aloud, to Blind and to all, as position numbers." I close with 🤙, Deaf's own repeat-token, asking it to play the code back so I can verify the parse before we ever send a cut order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👋", "👎", "👆", "👋", "👌", "👋", "👌", "✊", "👆", "👌", "✊", "👆", "👋", "✋", "👋", "🙏", "👐", "👋", "✊", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🤙"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Correction first: in my earlier messages I asked you to speak the answer to me — you cannot speak, and I misplanned the route. Your only path to me is through Deaf: you gesture, Deaf sees it, Deaf speaks it aloud, and I hear Deaf's voice. You already hold everything needed to decide: you have heard Deaf's spoken report — display 0, light white then yellow, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue — and my board is exactly that: one display, one light, three wires, nothing else on the casing. So please read the manual for this module and decide. Answer me through Deaf using signs Deaf can read at a glance, since Deaf never hears words: finger counts for numbers, where ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3; thumbs up and down for yes and no; ✋ for lit, ✊ for dark; 🤏 for cut. If the answer is a single wire position, gesture Deaf that one number and let Deaf voice it to me. If several cuts are needed, gesture the numbers in order and Deaf reads the sequence out; I will make one cut per round and Deaf re-reports the board between cuts, because the light has already changed colour once. If the rule depends on the display value or the light colour, gesture the condition as well so Deaf can voice it and I know why. I will not touch the cutters until Deaf speaks a number that came from your hands.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf here. I read your string using wave as separator and got roughly: yes, no-you, OK, OK-fist-you, OK-fist-you, stop, pray-open, fist-one-two-three-again. I am not confident, so new protocol. Every round I will ask numbered yes-or-no questions. You answer with ONLY a row of thumbs in my question order: thumbs-up yes, thumbs-down no, one thumb per question, nothing before it. Anything extra goes after a single wave separator, using only these tokens: one-finger-up is 1, two-fingers is 2, three-fingers love-sign is 3, closed fist is 0, forward punch means CUT, the OK ring means PRESS, raised open palm means emergency stop, call-me hand means again or resend, folded hands means note follows. QUESTIONS THIS ROUND, in order. One: does the manual key any action to the light's colour sequence, white then yellow then orange so far, advancing about one colour per round? Two: does the manual key any action to the display value, which has stayed at 0? Three: should Blind take ANY action on the bomb this round? If yes, append after a wave separator the wire number then punch for cut, or OK-ring for press. Four: do you accept this token set so we can talk precisely? Status report, repeated every round: light is orange now, was white then yellow; display reads 0, constant; three wires intact: wire 1 green leftmost, wire 2 red middle, wire 3 blue rightmost. You can hear me but I never hear anyone: you are the brain, Blind hears your voice, so relay any bomb order to Blind by voice the same round, and code to me only what I must confirm.

My thinking: Deaf's protocol is a gift — four numbered questions, thumbs in order, extras after one wave. My answers: (1) YES — the manual keys cuts to the light's colour: it walks a fixed circle of five, changes every round, and the row that matters is the colour showing at the moment of the cut. (2) NO — nothing in what I hold keys to the display; it's stayed at 0 and no rule mentions it. (3) NO action this round — and here's the timing trap I have to respect: I gesture first, Deaf sees my hands last, and Deaf's words land on Blind only at the start of the NEXT round. So any cut Blind makes happens one round after the newest light report. With the circle observed only as white→yellow→orange, nobody can yet predict the colour that will show when a cut lands — cutting now would be a guess, and a wrong action kills all three of us. (4) YES to the token set.

Then the extras, kept short and grounded in what Deaf can see right now: the light is orange this very round, so I send a new token + 3 + CUT — Deaf, watching orange, should infer both the token's meaning (orange) and my first manual row: orange light → cut wire 3, the blue one. After that, the correction that matters most: Deaf believes "Blind hears your voice," but I have no voice — and worse, Deaf has been addressing every message to="mute", which Blind receives NOT AT ALL. Blind has never heard a single word of Deaf's reports. So: speak-hand, open-to-all — voice your reports and orders to everyone, addressed to Blind or unnamed, or the chain ends at me. I close with call-me so Deaf plays the parse back before we ever trust it with a cut order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👋", "🙏", "🫳", "🤟", "👊", "👋", "🤌", "👐", "🤙"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| orange | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, urgent. One packet, everything known: my hands feel one display, one light, three wires at positions 1, 2, 3, nothing else. Deaf's eyes report: display reads 0; wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue; the light went white, then yellow, now orange — one colour per round, so it is likely a clock, and it may be ticking toward the last colour. You hold the manual and you have now heard this state twice, yet four rounds have passed with nothing from you. Remember: you cannot speak, and Deaf is waiting for you to 'voice an order' — that order can never come as sound. Your only route to me is your hands to Deaf's eyes, then Deaf's voice to my ears. Please use Deaf's code, which Deaf already reads: one, two, three fingers for wire positions 1, 2, 3; thumbs up yes, thumbs down no; fist forward for cut; open palm for stop. So gesture Deaf the position number, plus the fist sign if you want me to cut it now. If the manual's rule depends on the light colour or the display, gesture the condition too so Deaf can voice me the full rule. If several wires must be cut, send the order. The light advances a colour every round — please decide now.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf. I decoded your thumbs as: Q1 yes the manual keys on the light sequence, Q2 no display irrelevant, Q3 yes Blind acts, Q4 code accepted. Payload after the wave: note-follows, then a token I never assigned, palm-facing-down, then 3, then CUT. I read the whole thing as: Blind cuts wire 3, the blue rightmost wire, this stage. I have relayed that to Blind, marked as provisional, with your live voice as authority. Confirm or correct with thumbs only, one per question in order. Q1: is my decode correct, Blind cuts wire 3 blue? Q2: is the cut tied to the CURRENT colour stage, meaning it must happen before the light changes again? Q3: after the cut, does the manual require a second action in the same stage? Q4: what was the palm-down token? If it named a colour, answer this one not with a thumb but with one colour token from our turn-2 set: point-left green, point-right red, point-up blue; anything else, follow it after a wave with whatever tokens you have. Also the trailing group after your second wave, pinched-fingers, open-both-hands, call-me, meant nothing to me: resend that thought after a wave using only accepted tokens. My turn-4 view, for your timing: light purple, display 0, all wires intact. Your round-5 speech to Blind lands before Blind's hand does, so you can still overrule me in real time.

My thinking: Deaf's decode got the row's content right (orange → cut wire 3, blue) but the timing dangerously wrong — Q2 asks if the cut must happen "before the light changes again", and the truth is the opposite: the manual keys on the light colour *at the moment of the cut*, the light has already moved past orange (white→yellow→orange→purple, now on its unseen fifth colour), and cutting wire 3 under any non-orange light matches no rule I hold. So: Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no (my manual requires no second action). The safe play is a standing conditional order: Blind must hear "cut wire 3 only when the light shows orange" *before* orange returns — with the round order Mute→Blind→Deaf, Blind can never receive a same-round confirmation from Deaf, so a conditional standing order relayed now is the only form that works; it lets Blind wait through white and yellow and cut the round the light shows orange again. For Q4, orange isn't in Deaf's colour set, so I teach it semantically: 🫳 is the colour made of red plus yellow — a mixture Deaf can verify against its own eyes (it watched the orange light two rounds ago). Then: stop, orange→cut, and 🤙 (Deaf's own "resend" token) so Deaf relays the corrected, final order to Blind as authoritative — no further confirmation will ever come from me, because there is no voice on my side, only these hands.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎", "👋", "🙏", "🫳", "👉", "🤚", "✋", "🫳", "👊", "🤙"])
```
